comment: Telemetry, advertising, AI, widgets, web search, long paths. Section 8 of the v0.2 machine script.

rules.title: Minimal telemetry without disabling compatibility assessment
rules.summary: Diagnostic data level "Required" (the minimum for Pro), no feedback requests, no device name in the data, advertising ID off, error reports not sent, activity history not collected, the DiagTrack service set to Manual, the CEIP and Feedback tasks disabled.
rules.effect: The minimum data sending available on Pro. DiagTrack is intentionally not disabled: compatibility assessment for feature updates and Defender reporting need it.
rules.risk: Crash reports are not sent to Microsoft; local events 1000/1001 in the Application log remain.
rules.versions: AllowTelemetry=0 is treated as 1 on Pro; the Consolidator task may be missing on some 24H2 builds (WARN in the log).
rules.verify: Get-Service DiagTrack | Select-Object StartType; schtasks /Query /TN "\Microsoft\Windows\Customer Experience Improvement Program\UsbCeip"
rules.rollback: Delete the values; Set-Service DiagTrack -StartupType Automatic; schtasks /Change /Enable

values.title: Required: the minimum that Windows 11 Pro always sends
Security: Enterprise and Education only, on Pro it acts as "Required"

actions.name: Disabled
actions.why: local crash logs stay in Event Viewer

rules.title: No ads, preinstalled apps or automatic Teams installation (machine policies)
rules.summary: CloudContent policies (some apply only to Enterprise/Education and are kept because they are harmless), the Teams Chat icon hidden, automatic installation of personal Teams disabled.
rules.effect: On Pro the main working mechanism is the values in the default user profile (a separate rule in the profile group); this part enforces the same at the machine level.
rules.versions: DisableWindowsConsumerFeatures, DisableSoftLanding, DisableThirdPartySuggestions are Enterprise/Education only; DisableCloudOptimizedContent (10 20H2+) works on Pro, DisableConsumerAccountStateContent (11 22H2+) is not confirmed for Pro by the vendor; Windows Chat applies to 11 21H2-22H2.

rules.title: Copilot, Recall and Click to Do turned off
rules.summary: Copilot and WindowsAI policies: Recall (screen snapshots) is off and cannot be turned on by the user, Click to Do is off; the Recall feature is disabled if present.
rules.effect: No AI component takes screen snapshots or sends document contents. The Copilot app is removed by a separate rule in the apps group.
rules.versions: TurnOffWindowsCopilot since 23H2 (deprecated in 24H2, the copy in the user profile applies; the machine copy is not documented by Microsoft); DisableAIDataAnalysis since 24H2; AllowRecallEnablement and DisableClickToDo since the 2025 updates; the Recall feature only on Copilot+ PCs.

rules.title: Widgets and news feed turned off
rules.summary: The Windows 11 widgets board and the Windows 10 "News and interests" feed are disabled by policy.
rules.effect: No widgets button and no constantly open MSN web page with ads; the Widgets.exe process does not start.
rules.versions: Dsh policy since Windows 11 21H2; Windows Feeds for Windows 10 20H1+.

rules.title: No Bing web results in Start menu search
rules.summary: Start menu search finds only apps, files and settings; nothing is sent to Bing while typing.
rules.effect: Indexing and search in File Explorer and Outlook are not affected (the WSearch service is left untouched).
rules.versions: DisableSearchBoxSuggestions since Windows 10 2004; Cortana has been removed from Windows 11 (the policy is harmless).
rules.verify: Searching Start for the word "weather" shows no web results.

rules.title: Long path support (more than 260 characters)
rules.summary: Programs with the longPathAware manifest (PowerShell 7, Git, modern archivers) work with paths longer than 260 characters.
rules.effect: File Explorer and older programs keep the limit; harmless.
rules.versions: Windows 10 1607+.

rules.title: Recall and Click to Do turned off in the user profile too
rules.summary: User copies of the policies: Recall does not save screen snapshots, Click to Do is unavailable.
rules.effect: Complements the machine rule "Copilot, Recall and Click to Do turned off": the user cannot turn these features on for themselves.
rules.versions: Windows 11 24H2 (26100.3915) and later; the features themselves exist only on Copilot+ PCs, on other PCs the values have no effect.
rules.rollback: Delete the values in the user profile.
rules.note: 28.09.2026, customer list MoreOptions: Windows AI (card 19, section "Windows AI")

rules.title: No AI agent in Settings search
rules.summary: Search in the "Settings" app works without the AI agent: by index and semantic search.
rules.effect: Queries in "Settings" are not processed by the AI agent that changes settings on its own.
rules.versions: Pre-release policy: present in the Windows 11 25H2 (26200) templates; the vendor does not yet confirm that it works on Pro.

rules.title: Block AI agents from connecting to apps (agent connectors)
rules.summary: Agent connectors (MCP servers through which AI agents work with apps and files) are forcibly turned off.
rules.effect: Windows AI agents get no access to the user's apps and data through connectors. Replaces the values DisableAgentConnectors, DisableAgentWorkspaces and DisableRemoteAgentConnectors from the list: Windows has no such policies.
rules.versions: Pre-release policy: present in the Windows 11 25H2 (26200) templates; the agent workspace is turned on only by an administrator in "Settings", there is no separate policy for it.

rules.title: Apps are blocked from Windows text and image generation features
rules.summary: Apps cannot use the built-in Windows AI models ("Text and image generation" in the privacy settings); the user cannot change this.
rules.effect: Notepad, Photos, Snipping Tool, Outlook and other apps do not call the Windows AI models. Replaces the list's internal ConsentStore values generativeAI and systemAIModels and the old policy name LetAppsAccessGenerativeAI.
rules.versions: Windows 11 24H2 and later (the policy is in the AppPrivacy template of build 26200).
rules.verify: Settings -> Privacy & security -> Text and image generation: the toggle is locked.

rules.title: Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot without microphone access
rules.summary: The Copilot and Microsoft 365 (Office Hub) apps get no microphone access, even if they are reinstalled; other apps still ask the user.
rules.effect: Voice input in Copilot is unavailable. Replaces the list's internal ConsentStore permissions for these two apps with a documented policy.
rules.versions: Windows 10 1607 and later.
rules.verify: Settings -> Privacy & security -> Microphone: access for Copilot is denied by the organization.

rules.title: Paint without AI features
rules.summary: Image Creator, Cocreator, generative fill, generative erase and background removal are hidden in Paint.
rules.effect: Drawings and descriptions are not sent to a cloud image generator. The first three policies are documented by Microsoft; DisableGenerativeErase and DisableRemoveBackground come from the customer's list and are not yet documented by Microsoft.
rules.versions: Windows 11 22H2 (22621.4870) and 24H2 (26100.3360) and later. Policy path: SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\Paint (the list gives the wrong path SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Paint).

rules.title: Notepad without AI features
rules.summary: Copilot features in Notepad are turned off: rewrite, summarize and similar.
rules.effect: Text from Notepad is not sent to cloud AI models.
rules.versions: Windows 11 22H2 and later with Notepad 11.2503.16.0 and later.

rules.title: No Microsoft 365 Copilot setup screen at sign-in
rules.summary: After signing in to Windows, the screen that offers to pin Microsoft 365 Copilot is not shown.
rules.effect: Fewer promotional screens after updates. This does not turn off Copilot itself.
rules.versions: Pre-release policy: present in the Windows 11 25H2 (26200) templates.

rules.title: No typing statistics (Typing insights)
rules.summary: Windows does not collect statistics on autocorrections and suggestions while typing.
rules.effect: No local typing statistics are kept. This is neither telemetry nor generative AI: a rule from the customer's list.
rules.versions: Windows 10 1803 and later; the value is not documented by Microsoft as a policy, it matches the "Typing insights" toggle in Settings.
rules.rollback: Settings -> Time & language -> Typing -> Typing insights.

rules.title: Telemetry: Windows settings state at the "Required" level
rules.summary: Values that the "Diagnostics & feedback" page shows: the "Required" level is selected and cannot be raised.
rules.effect: The Settings app does not offer to turn on optional diagnostic data. Values from the customer's list; this is not a policy but the state of the settings page, the AllowTelemetry policy plays the main role.
rules.versions: All releases of Windows 10 and 11; the values are not documented by Microsoft as a policy.
rules.note: 28.09.2026, customer list MoreOptions: telemetry, advertising, search, speech (card 19)

rules.title: Telemetry: user copy of the data level policy
rules.summary: The diagnostic data level policy is also set in the user profile: "Required".
rules.effect: If both the machine and the user policy are set, the stricter one applies. Value from the customer's list.
rules.versions: Windows 10 1507 and later.

rules.title: Telemetry: no notifications about data level changes
rules.summary: Windows does not show a notification about diagnostic data settings at first sign-in and after the level changes.
rules.effect: The user sees no offers to raise the data level. A documented replacement for the ShowedToastAtLevel value from the list.
rules.versions: Windows 10 1803 and later, Pro.

rules.title: Telemetry: limit logs and memory dumps
rules.summary: Windows does not collect additional diagnostic logs, and error reports contain only minimal dumps.
rules.effect: Less data about how the PC works goes to Microsoft. At the "Required" level the policies change nothing, but they guard against optional data being turned on by accident.
rules.versions: Windows 11 21H2 and later, Pro.

rules.title: Application Telemetry turned off
rules.summary: The mechanism that tracks how apps use Windows components is turned off.
rules.effect: Information about app usage is not collected. Microsoft does not describe any link to the compatibility check before feature updates; the rule does not touch the DisableInventory policy, which does concern that check.
rules.versions: Windows 10 and 11, Pro; machine policy only (the user copy from the list does not exist).

rules.title: Steps Recorder turned off
rules.summary: Steps Recorder, which takes a screenshot with every click, is unavailable.
rules.effect: "Tech support" scammers cannot ask the user to record and send their actions. Microsoft has declared the tool deprecated.
rules.versions: Windows 10 and 11, Pro.

rules.title: Apps are blocked from diagnostic information about other apps
rules.summary: Store apps do not get information about how other apps run; the user cannot change this.
rules.effect: Replaces the internal ConsentStore appDiagnostics value from the list with a documented policy.
rules.versions: Windows 10 1703 and later, Pro.

rules.title: Feedback frequency: never
rules.summary: "Never" is selected in the user profile for the Windows feedback frequency.
rules.effect: Complements the machine policy DoNotShowFeedbackNotifications; the user copy of this policy from the list does not exist, so a user setting is written instead.
rules.versions: All releases of Windows 10 and 11.

rules.title: Lock screen without "Windows spotlight" and suggested content
rules.summary: Windows Spotlight pictures do not change on the lock screen, general suggested content is turned off.
rules.effect: The lock screen shows a regular picture without ads. SubscribedContentEnabled is taken from the customer's list; Microsoft does not describe its exact effect.
rules.versions: Windows 10 and 11; user settings, not policies (the Spotlight policy is not supported on Pro).

rules.title: No tailored tips or third-party app suggestions
rules.summary: User policies: diagnostic data is not used for tailored tips, third-party apps are not suggested.
rules.effect: Fewer app ads in the Start menu, in tips and on the lock screen.
rules.versions: Windows 10 1607 and 1703 and later, Pro.

rules.title: No account notifications in Settings
rules.summary: The "Settings" app does not show offers to sign in with a Microsoft account and connect its services.
rules.effect: Fewer ads for the Microsoft account and subscriptions. The value is not documented by Microsoft as a policy, it matches a toggle in Settings.
rules.versions: Windows 11.

rules.title: Advertising ID turned off in the new settings store too
rules.summary: The advertising ID toggle is turned off in the Windows 11 settings store (CPSS).
rules.effect: Complements the DisabledByGroupPolicy policy and the AdvertisingInfo Enabled value. Value from the customer's list, not documented by Microsoft.
rules.versions: Windows 11 23H2 and later (not confirmed by the vendor).

rules.title: Windows Search without the cloud, search highlights and location
rules.summary: Windows Search does not search OneDrive and other clouds, does not show "search highlights" and does not use location.
rules.effect: Queries stay on the computer, and the search box shows no promotional pictures of the day.
rules.versions: Windows 10 1709 and later; search highlights since Windows 11 22H2. Pro.

rules.title: Search without cloud content and history (user profile)
rules.summary: The user's search toggles are turned off: cloud content from Microsoft and Entra ID accounts, search highlights, search history on this device.
rules.effect: Matches the machine search policies and turns off the local query history. Values from the customer's list; they match the toggles in Settings.
rules.versions: Windows 11; user settings, not policies.

rules.title: Do not track app launches for the Start menu and search
rules.summary: Windows does not remember which apps the user launches for the Start menu lists and search results.
rules.effect: No list of most used apps is kept in the Start menu.
rules.versions: All releases of Windows 10 and 11.

rules.title: No cloud speech recognition or handwriting improvement
rules.summary: Users cannot turn on cloud speech recognition services, and handwriting and typing data is not sent to improve recognition.
rules.effect: Voice and typed text do not go to Microsoft.
rules.risk: Cloud voice typing and dictation do not work.
rules.versions: Windows 10 1507 and 1607 and later, Pro.

rules.title: Speech and input personalization turned off in the user profile
rules.summary: Cloud speech recognition and the personal dictionary for handwriting and typing are turned off in the user profile.
rules.effect: Windows does not collect handwriting samples, typed text and contacts for the dictionary. The user copy of the AllowInputPersonalization policy from the list does not exist, so user settings are written instead.
rules.risk: Handwriting recognition does not adapt to the user.
rules.versions: All releases of Windows 10 and 11.

rules.title: Narrator without online services
rules.summary: Narrator does not send images and pages to the cloud for image descriptions, page titles and popular links.
rules.effect: Screen content does not go to Microsoft while Narrator is running.
rules.versions: Windows 11.

rules.title: Narrator without extensions
rules.summary: Narrator extensions (scripts for Excel, Outlook and other programs) are turned off.
rules.effect: Value from the customer's list. This is not telemetry: the extensions improve how Narrator works in programs.
rules.risk: Narrator works worse in Excel and Outlook: this matters for blind employees.
rules.versions: Recent Windows 11 builds.

rules.title: Do not run companion programs of driver installers (co-installers)
rules.summary: When a device is connected, Windows installs the driver but does not run the vendor's companion programs from the driver package.
rules.effect: Closes a class of attacks in which a vendor program (the Razer Synapse case, 2021) runs with SYSTEM rights when a device is connected. Drivers from Windows Update keep arriving.
rules.risk: Vendor utilities for old printers, scanners and gaming devices will have to be installed manually; check on a test PC with the organization's devices.
rules.versions: All releases of Windows 10 and 11; the value is widely used but not documented on Microsoft Learn. Since 2023 Microsoft does not sign packages with co-installers.
rules.note: 28.09.2026, customer list MoreOptions: drivers and devices (card 19)

rules.title: Do not download device apps and icons from the internet
rules.summary: Windows does not use device metadata to download the vendors' related apps and their icons.
rules.effect: No vendor programs without the user's knowledge. Microsoft retired the device metadata service in 2025; the policy guards against leftovers.
rules.versions: Windows 10 1809 and later, Pro.
